subject.title: fix: keep broken SSH sandbox refs agent-scoped

question: Should disabled-agent SSH SecretRefs remain inactive by default, or may Gateway startup materialize them solely to preserve possible remote-runtime lifecycle access?
rationale: The PR trades the documented inactive-secret boundary for lifecycle manageability, potentially executing providers and loading credentials for disabled sandboxes; that security and compatibility tradeoff requires explicit owner intent.

options.title: Preserve Inactive Secrets
options.body: Resolve disabled-agent credentials only when a concrete existing SSH runtime is being inspected or removed, preserving the current startup contract.

options.title: Accept Eager Materialization
options.body: Explicitly approve startup materialization for disabled SSH configurations, document the expanded active surface, and require upgrade and security proof.

options.title: Pause Lifecycle Expansion
options.body: Land only agent-owner isolation and ambient-fallback prevention while tracking disabled-runtime lifecycle handling separately.

recommendation.title: Preserve Inactive Secrets
recommendation.body: Resolve disabled-agent credentials only when a concrete existing SSH runtime is being inspected or removed, preserving the current startup contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The sandbox lifecycle design and recent ownership history are concentrated in this contributor's merged work, with security-owner review still required.
